A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support comparison, including matching retained material across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original LLM fine-tuning experiments, benchmark evaluations, and ablations, including Table 3, Figure 3, and Appendix A.2.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds comparator results and filtering and reward-scaling ablations in Appendix B.

M1.justification: v3 introduces an SFT-regularized theoretical DPO variant in Algorithm 1 and Eq. (A.9). The practical two-goal relabeling procedure and highest-score inference remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish that the empirical models used this additional regularizer.

E1.justification: Both versions retain UltraFeedback, the on-policy response-generation scenarios, three instruction-following benchmarks, and six academic benchmarks. The added filtering and reward-scaling experiments stay within existing dataset and task coverage.

E2.justification: v3 adds NCA-P, NCA-R, InfoNCA-P, and InfoNCA-R to the Zephyr-SFT comparison in Figure 4 and Table 12; the table abbreviates InfoNCA as INCA. Existing DPA, SteerLM, DPO, RPO, and on-policy comparators are retained.

E3.justification: Appendix B.3 introduces controls that exclude high- or low-reward rejected-response augmentations and linearly rescale rewards from 1–10 to 1–5 or 1–100. Previously reported benchmark settings, model configurations, and training hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds two targeted ablations testing the contribution of high-quality rejected responses and sensitivity to reward scale (Tables 14–15). The existing inference-goal ablation moves from v2 Table 7 to v3 Table 13 with unchanged results; other original analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version specifies experimental run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedures. The added tables continue to report point estimates without introducing an uncertainty-estimation practice.

E6.justification: v3 Table 12 newly reports Zephyr comparison LC win rates, including 14.83 for INCA-R and 16.66 for Ours. Tables 14–15 add filtering and scaling outcomes. Existing academic and full instruction-following benchmark scores remain unchanged, including v2 Table 12 versus v3 Table 11.

T1.justification: Section 4 replaces the exact-match indicator and absolute-error formulation with a negative squared-error reward. v3 adds Theorem 4.1 and Appendix A, including a goal-conditioned Bradley–Terry formulation, realizability, regularity and partial-coverage assumptions, and a claimed N^-1/2-type suboptimality bound with supporting derivations and lemmas.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same reward-augmentation, benchmark-improvement, unlearning, and on-policy SOTA claims. v3 shortens the conclusion, but the omitted summary claims remain in the abstract and introduction, preserving their meaning and scope.

C2.justification: v3 interprets its new theorem as explaining empirical effectiveness through global convergence, with the appendix discussing coverage and distribution shift. Appendix B.3 newly argues robustness to reward scaling and suggests possible benefits from a 1–100 scale. Existing unlearning and feedback-noise interpretations remain.

D1.justification: v3 removes direct checkpoint URL footnotes for the evaluated models, including SPPO and Zephyr-SFT. Model names, the project code URL, prompt templates, reward normalization, and existing DPO hyperparameters are retained. The new ablations describe linear rescaling but do not specify high/low filtering thresholds.

R1.justification: v3 substantially expands theoretical positioning by claiming stronger global guarantees than goal-conditioned supervised RL, explicitly contrasting with Ghosh et al. (2019) and Yang et al. (2022). It adds supporting offline-RLHF and partial-coverage literature, alongside Chen et al. (2024) for the new NCA/InfoNCA comparisons.

P1.justification: Changes include expanded authorship and affiliations, revised subsection headings and explanations, an expanded Table 5 caption, and a shortened conclusion. The experimental appendix becomes Appendix B and receives the moved prompt-control ablation. Most existing prose and the main section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds an algorithm box and three result tables, expands illustrative Table 1, and adds comparator markers and legend entries to Figure 4. Figure 2's lower panels are rearranged, and several existing displays are resized or relocated. The overall visual format remains consistent.

improvement.justification: The added NCA/InfoNCA comparisons and focused ablations strengthen empirical support. However, the new theoretical guarantee concerns an SFT-regularized variant and contains unresolved inconsistencies: Eq. (A.10)'s denominator cancels to zero, while Eq. (A.19) reverses the regularizer sign from Eq. (A.9). These empirical benefits and problems in the claimed theoretical support prevent a reliable net-quality judgment.
